title: An arrival rate and a queue
hook: A toy line has spare service capacity. What changes when arrivals pass the service rate?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Identify the sign of net flow when arrivals cross fixed service capacity.

misconception: A service can absorb indefinitely any arrival rate close to its stated capacity.
objective: Identify the sign of net flow when arrivals cross fixed service capacity.

claims.text: Original stipulated feedback model: A inputs [0, 5, 6, 6] yield 0; B inputs [0, 7, 6, 6] yield 6. Prediction correct option 6. A leaves {A} waiting jobs; B leaves {B}. The same six-job service can absorb five arrivals but accumulates one per round when seven arrive. Fixed arrivals and service only; no stochastic near-capacity queueing law or utilization nonlinearity is shown.

claims.text: A toy queue starts empty, receives 9 and serves 7 each round for four rounds. Waiting jobs? Net inflow is two jobs each round; four rounds accumulate eight.
